videos.titulo: What Explains the Yield Variation in KNCA11? | Alternative Assets Live Clip
videos.descricao:
Low returns in the fund may reflect temporary allocation and inflation factors, without indicating deterioration in the loan portfolio.
In the live stream, we explained why the monthly return of KNCA11 was below historical averages, despite the portfolio remaining 100% performing. The first factor was the temporary increase in the cash position after prepayments of loan operations. While this cash awaits reallocation, its return tends to be lower than that of the assets originally held in the portfolio.

Prepayments, on the other hand, do not necessarily represent a negative sign: they may reflect companies in a healthier financial situation and still generate a compensation premium for the fund. We also addressed the impact of a lower IPCA reading on assets indexed to real interest rates. As a significant portion of the portfolio tracks inflation, the recent slowdown in the index temporarily reduced the distributed return.

videos.titulo: Portfolio Holds Value Despite Volatility | KNHF - Aug/26
videos.descricao:
Real estate funds fell sharply in August, and KNHF was not immune: while the IFIX index retreated 1.47% in the month — amidst a historic sequence of eleven consecutive declines in the Ibovespa, the worst since 2023, driven by fiscal uncertainty surrounding the elections in Brazil and pressure from commodities and interest rates abroad — KNHF's market capitalization fell 2.69%. In this video, management explains why this movement reflects a risk premium embedded by the market, and not a worsening of fundamentals: the fund's net asset value appreciated 1.10% in the period, widening the discount between the market price and the real value of the portfolio — currently, with approximately 40% of the portfolio in IPCA+ CRIs yielding close to IPCA+12.80% p.a. and another 16% in CDI+6.20% p.a. at the current market price. The team also details the movements in the CRI and FoF portfolio, the absence of vacancies in corporate office space on Faria Lima, the progress in the structured payment for the São Luís Building, and the maintenance of the distribution of R$ 1.00 per share, to be paid on September 11th. If you are a shareholder or investor in REITs, understand why the IFIX correction may represent an opportunity to enter at a discount.

By Yago Costa, from the Investor Relations team.

videos.titulo: Infrastructure Fund Yields | KDIF and KNDI - Aug/26
videos.descricao:
Infrastructure Fund Yields in Focus: In this video, we present the August 2026 results of the Kinea Infra (KDIF) fund, indexed to the IPCA (Brazilian inflation index), and the Estratégia Infra (KNDI) fund, indexed to the CDI (Brazilian interbank deposit rate), in addition to our analysis of the private credit environment and incentivized debentures in Brazil. KDIF reported a yield of R$1.00 per share in August, stable compared to July, even with 9% fewer business days in the month and a slight deflation in the IPCA. This result was possible thanks to the use of the fund's historical profit reserve, a practice already adopted in previous seasonal months to provide greater predictability for investors. KNDI paid R$1.00 per share, a reduction compared to R$1.10 in July, directly reflecting the fewer business days; the fund continues with an allocation of 65% of its capacity, with expectations of reaching full allocation by the end of the year, which should increase the potential for income distribution. We also explained why, given high interest rates for a prolonged period and signs of a slowdown in economic activity, we have adopted a more cautious stance and more gradual allocations, prioritizing opportunities in the secondary market, highlighting that the average KDIF premium is 1.5% above the government bond, well above the average of 0.3% for the incentivized debenture market measured by the ANBIMA index.

videos.titulo: Ibovespa Drops and Recovers Everything | Equity Funds - Aug/26
videos.descricao:
The Ibovespa ended August 2026 practically stable, but the month was marked by two contrasting fortnights: a 6% drop at the beginning, with the trading session of August 11th falling 2.5%, the largest daily drop in five months, amidst noise of foreign capital outflow, followed by a strong recovery that erased losses and maintained the accumulated gain of over 10% for the year. Abroad, the S&P 500 rose 2.5%, but with significant dispersion among sectors, while Kevin Warsh, chairman of the Federal Reserve, reinforced the commitment to the 2% inflation target even with still loose financial conditions, and second-quarter profits for American companies grew by about 30%, showing that the strength of the results goes beyond artificial intelligence. In Brazil, the Copom (Monetary Policy Committee) cut the Selic rate to 14%, marking its fourth consecutive cut, maintaining a contractionary tone, while the earnings season disappointed and the electoral scenario heated up, with the gap between the two main candidates narrowing towards a tight presidential race. Kinea's equity funds closed August in line with the Ibovespa (Brazilian stock market index), without significant sectoral highlights, and for September, attention remains focused on the Copom's potential for rate cuts, long-term US interest rates, and the acceleration of the election campaign.

By Rafael Oliveira, manager of Kinea's equity funds.

videos.titulo: High Yield Puts Pressure on Spreads | Private Credit Funds - Aug/26
videos.descricao:
High Yield was the only segment to widen its spread in the ANBIMA debenture index in August, while High Grade and Mid-Yield remained stable with slight closures. The widening of the IDA (ANBIMA Debenture Index) came almost entirely from the negative performance of Hapvida's bonds. In this video, we explain why we expect carry in line with current spreads for High Grade and Mid-Yield, why we remain selectively optimistic about closing opportunities in High Yield (a class still displaced from pre-opening levels from February to April, the third largest in the IDA's recent history), and why Kinea's portfolio had no exposure to any of the names that entered judicial or extrajudicial reorganization during this period — the result of a company-by-company analysis within the universe of relevant issuers in the industry.

By Ivan Fernandes, manager of Kinea's Private Credit funds.

videos.titulo: US Interest Rates Pressure Brazil | Fixed Income Fund Update - Aug/26
videos.descricao:
Long-term interest rates in the US remain under pressure due to strong capital demand from the artificial intelligence investment cycle, coupled with US fiscal deficits—a structural effect that spreads across the yield curve of several countries, including Brazil. In this video, we explain why the Fed may keep interest rates stable even against this backdrop, how the proximity of the Brazilian elections has increased volatility and reduced foreign appetite for domestic risk, and why, despite favorable inflation and activity data in Brazil, the Central Bank should act cautiously until the 2027 fiscal and electoral scenario is defined, opening space, in our view, for a resumption of interest rate cuts after that period. We also discuss why we remain positioned for lower rates in countries with greater economic slack, such as Mexico, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom, the inflationary risks stemming from oil and gas due to conflicts in the Middle East, and our long position in the dollar and Korean won and short position in the euro, reflecting AI-linked growth in Korea in the face of structural and fiscal weaknesses in Europe.

By Roberto Elaiuy, from the fixed income fund management team at Kinea.
